target_customer: Brick and mortar retailers and e-commerce brands such as florists, meal kits and pharmacies that want same-day delivery under their own brand
problem: Small merchants could not match Amazon's same-day delivery and lacked a branded, affordable last mile option.
business_model: Per delivery fees for white label same-day delivery using crowdsourced drivers, with Shopify and Squarespace integrations

founders.name: Jaden Pereira
education: University of Waterloo, biology (student when he co-founded, per BetaKit)
founders.background_notes: Co-founded in 2018 as a Waterloo student; BetaKit states he was 22 at the time.

founders.name: Aaron Paul
education: University of Waterloo, engineering (studying, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC bio says he has been entrepreneurial since Grade 9 selling study notes.

founders.name: Joe Rhew
prior_employers: Uber Eats Canada (head of marketplace operations)
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and COO in the March 2021 BetaKit article; not on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Dispatch, routing and merchant integrations are standard software; the difficulty is operating a reliable driver network.

defensibility.rationale: Courier networks and white label front ends are copyable; density of drivers and merchant integrations are the only edges.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch in April 2021 describes Tyltgo as a white label version of Uber Eats; no incumbent moved against it according to sources, and a routing partner blog says it reached profitability.

market_need_then: Pandemic demand for delivery: TechCrunch reports revenue grew 2,000 percent from December 2019 to December 2020 and headcount went from two to nine in 2020.

identity.voice_and_tone: Small business empowerment against Amazon (TechCrunch headline framing)

branding.brand_signature: White label: merchants deliver under their own brand

brand_strength.rationale: Invented, unusual spelling that is hard to type; the product is white label so end customers see the merchant's brand, not Tyltgo.

outcome_analysis: TyltGO rode pandemic delivery demand, reporting 2,000 percent revenue growth in 2020, and raised a C$2.3M seed in March 2021. It remains active at 15 people with a later small round reported by one aggregator. The white label model means low brand pull, and growth appears moderate rather than venture scale so far.
notes: The company site returned HTTP 503 so was not read. Seed was C$2.3M (US$1.8M) per BetaKit, confirmed by TechCrunch, the University of Waterloo (C$2.3M, April 2021) and FreightWaves. CB Insights lists five rounds, $1.99M total and a Seed IV in July 2023 (Brighter Capital); that is a single aggregator so it is not recorded. Competitors list empty: the articles name only Amazon, HelloFresh and Uber Eats as comparisons, not direct rivals; Shippie and FlashBox appear on undated directory pages and Swyft only on CB Insights, so none qualify as dated sources. Founding year varies: 2018 per BetaKit and TechCrunch (July 2018), 2019 per YC and CB Insights.
